ai.description: *Uropeltis ocellata* reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown with yellow-bordered black ocelli along the body and a blunt, shield-like tail tip. The venter is yellow with dark cross-bars.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis ocellata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, yellowish-white ocellated (eye-like) spot on each scale along its lateral body.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis ocellata* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ocellated Earth Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil to feed on earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis ocellata* is viviparous, typically producing a small litter of 3–8 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with births recorded between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ocellated Earth Snake is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
